Observed two demos and a successful test solve (one wrong submission before identifying exact pattern).

## Pattern
- The background contains vertical color-2 divider cells/lines. A marker is a 3x3 ring of color 3 with a color-2 center, centered on one of those vertical divider columns.
- Each ring generates a horizontal stripe in color 1 on its center row: fill every non-divider, non-marker cell across the full row with 1. Keep all original 2s and all 3s unchanged.
- On the rows immediately above and below that ring's center row, place color 1 in the two cells immediately to the left and right of **every** vertical divider 2. Keep the divider 2 itself unchanged. This forms 3-cell-wide bands centered on each vertical divider, except where original marker 3s already occupy cells.
- Apply independently for every 3-ring marker. Preserve original grid dimensions and all source 2/3 cells.

Equivalent construction when divider columns are c: for each marker center row r, set all cells in row r except original 2/3 cells to 1; in rows r-1 and r+1, set c-1 and c+1 to 1 for every divider column c, leaving all 2/3 as they were. Where markers overlap or already contain 3s, retain 3s. Do not paint entire neighboring rows.

## Demo evidence
1. 10x10 demo: divider row (all 2s) and ring centered at row 1, col 5. Output puts 1s at center-column c5 on the rows between the ring and divider/edge, plus 3-wide side bands on the divider row; original 2s/3s remain.
2. 15x12 demo: divider columns c3 and c9, rings centered at (r2,c3) and (r11,c9). Output has full horizontal color-1 stripes at both marker center rows, excluding divider cells and preserving rings; the rows above/below each marker get 1s on either side of both divider columns, unless the source ring's 3s occupy those cells.
